definition: The death of a woman during pregnancy, childbirth, or shortly after, from causes related to the pregnancy.
The number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births - the standard measure of how risky pregnancy is.
Deaths caused by pregnancy or birth itself, such as eclampsia, bleeding, infection or obstructed labour.
Deaths from other conditions made worse by pregnancy, such as anaemia, heart disease, malaria or HIV.
Dangerously high blood pressure in pregnancy that leads to seizures; often preceded by pre-eclampsia.
Heavy, life-threatening bleeding during or after childbirth.
A severe infection during pregnancy, birth or the period after, often after unsafe abortion or prolonged labour.
A tear in the wall of the womb, usually caused by obstructed labour; often fatal without surgery.
The World Health Organization’s coding system for classifying diseases and causes of death.
Births per 1,000 people in a year.
A birth that takes place in a health facility rather than at home.
Women aged 15-49, the group at risk of maternal death.
